speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. How old is the infant, and can you describe exactly what activities seem to trigger the stridor and wheezing?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Has the stridor been present since birth, and does the child appear to have difficulty swallowing or drooling excessively? I also need to know if there is any history of choking episodes during feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the relief with neck extension and worsening with flexion, does the infant have a history of cyanosis or near-drowning episodes during these spells? Also, is there any family history of similar breathing issues or congenital heart defects?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical or surgical history. Born full term with no complications during birth. Social history: First child in the family. Lives with both parents. No exposure to smoking or pets in the household.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of stridor worsening with neck flexion and improving with extension strongly suggests a vascular ring compressing the trachea. To confirm this anatomical anomaly, I will order specific imaging. REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray. REQUEST TEST: Barium_Swallow. REQUEST IMAGES.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_X-ray: Evidence of tracheal compression and a vascular ring suggestive of a double aortic arch. Barium_Swallow: Compression of the esophagus and trachea consistent with a vascular ring. Echocardiogram: Confirmatory findings of a double aortic arch.

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging and echocardiogram confirm a double aortic arch compressing the trachea and esophagus. DIAGNOSIS READY: Double Aortic Arch.
